items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: Well I was with Woody Herman only for a short bit, I just went out to help Frank Tiberi and they just called me up as a sub.

ctx.x: Okay so I went back to Berklee. Jimmy Mosher was the alto player who had just gotten off the summer tour with Buddy Rich. He did the “Away We Go” Jackie Gleason special, but he came back to Berklee to teach. So they put me in his ensemble, and I was in for about two weeks. On the second week we all go to a bar afterwards on a Friday night rehearsal — me, Lynn Bivvy — well Lynn had left already. And Lynn had gone on the © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

road — Lynn Biviano, the trumpet player. And he was out with Woody Herman. And so Jimmy Mosher was hanging out with Johnny in the bar and he said, “You know you’ve been in school too long.” He said, “You should go out on the road.” And we’re all drinking. And he said, “There’s a job opening with Buddy Rich. I’m going to make a call and get you the gig.” This was while we’re all drinking on Friday. So Monday morning comes around and I see Jimmy Mosher and I say, “Okay where’s that gig with Buddy Rich?” He said,…

items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: I had a record company out in California, one of Woody’s recordings. The guy said, “Well we don’t pay that kind of money for arrangements” and you know, “this is something you should be happy, you’re going to get your stuff on a Woody Herman record.”

ctx.x: Do you remember if at some point, you mentioned the stock arrangements, and you’re playing all this different music. Did you have this epiphany or an aha moment, like I could do this? I could arrange. I want to do that.

Well I don’t know if it really was an epiphany moment but I remember when we started getting interested in jazz, real jazz, not the Dixieland or the swing stuff that we were playing as kids, when we got into high school and we all of a sudden heard Miles Davis and we heard all of these great artists, I was the one who took them off the records. I have, for some reason I have the ability to hear all those inner lines and then write them down. I was the one who did that. So we could copy “So What” you know the…
Was your father, I’m not sure how to put this, was he living out a way of life that he wished he had had as a professional musician?
